ai_patterns_removed: translationese register stripped from Draupadi's appeal: 'his words fraught with virtue and profit', 'the scriptures excepting only a Brahmana, the preceptor of all orders', 'Such a deed would become the son of Pritha' — every argument kept in order and meaning (five villages refused, no need to ride to Hastinapura, warriors meet severity with severity, sin of sparing the guilty, the three-fold deed)

unglossed names made plain: 'the son of Dhritarashtra' -> 'Duryodhana'; Srinjayas/Panchalas/Vrishnis collapsed to one readable identity plea; 'Fie to Arjuna's bowmanship... fie to Bhima's might' -> 'Shame on Arjuna's bowmanship... and shame on Bhima's might'
piling gloss trimmed: single 'Satyaki, of Krishna's own clan' replaces the unexplained 'mighty car-warrior' tag carried from the source register
child_friendly_changes: opening anchor added: the five brothers named, their kingdom lost to cousin Duryodhana at loaded dice; Draupadi identified as 'wife of the five brothers'; Krishna as 'their cousin and friend'
loose hair tied to the dice game ('as it had since the dice game') so a first reader reads the unbound tresses as a sign, not a mystery
Dhrishtadyumna kept as 'your dear friend' and Abhimanyu glossed as 'Arjuna's son'; Bhishma glossed as 'grandsire of the Kurus'; brahmin glossed as 'priest and teacher of every order'
cow-elephant simile kept but registered plainly ('heavy and slow as a cow elephant')
Sanjaya glossed as 'the king's messenger' at first mention (named messenger from the source, previously unexplained)
risk: 'Such a deed would become the son of Pritha, add to Krishna's glory...' (Ganguli 5.82) is textually ambiguous and Pritha is never explained in the source passage — rendered 'Such a deed would honour my husbands' (the sons of Pritha are her husbands), keeping the three-fold claim. Srinjayas (a second name for the Panchala host) rendered 'their allies'; Panchalas and Vrishnis kept in the identity plea. Boon, freeing of the Pandavas, and exile-after-freedom kept exactly.

ai_patterns_removed: single ~150-word recap paragraph split into three and shorn of its source-listing rhythm ('how... how... how...'); every element kept: five villages refused, hair seized, assembly insult, 'save me' cry, boon, exile
epithet 'the lotus-eyed one' -> plain 'Krishna' where it named him as answerer
clever double line reduced: 'answered her cry with cloth; now with an oath' kept once, 'the two were of the same fabric' dropped
two long interpretive paragraphs on the oath compressed to one; 'the order of the world would break before his word would' kept
child_friendly_changes: Dussasana glossed as 'Duryodhana's brother' on first use
'the ladies of Bharata's race' rendered 'the women of the Kuru house' (Bharata = the dynasty's ancestor; matches the story's own title)
'the mountains of Himavat' rendered 'the mountains of the Himalaya'; 'my words can never be futile' -> 'my words can never come to nothing'
identity recap kept whole ('wife of five heroes; mother of five warrior sons bound to Krishna as Abhimanyu was')

ai_patterns_removed: translationese speech smoothed throughout: 'It behoveth', 'even as Prajapati is the friend of both the gods and the Asuras', 'Suyodhana', 'endued', 'the sinful expedient of deceitful dice' — argument order and every idea kept
'their immediate destruction preferable' (draft's ambiguous referent) rephrased neutrally as 'if Krishna judged that the time for war had come'
patronymic 'Suyodhana deserved death at my hands' -> 'Duryodhana deserved to die at my hands' (same man, common name)
child_friendly_changes: opening anchor added: 'the five Pandava brothers... Duryodhana, who sat in Hastinapura, the city of the Kurus, had taken their kingdom from them with loaded dice'
Nakula glossed as 'his younger brother Bhima's... Nakula'; Kshatriya rendered 'born to the sword'; Prajapati rendered 'the creator of all beings' and Asuras 'demons'
closing kept as quiet faith-image ('the waiting itself had become a kind of faith') rather than a moral
risk: Arjuna's speech preserved step by step (doubts on easy peace, human prowess needing exertion, peace properly proposed, friend of both houses, Draupadi insult borne with patience, Duryodhana deaf to counsel 'like seed sown in barren soil'). No item dropped.

ai_patterns_removed: Ganguli-register speech recast: 'It behoveth thee', 'auspicious and beneficial counsels fraught with virtue and profit', 'victim of his fate' -> plain speech; Krishna's three-clause acceptance kept ('what is right, what may benefit us, and what is good for the Kurus')

chariot catalogue rewritten from source-prose into two plain paragraphs — every element kept: blazing car, sun-and-moon wheels, painted moons/fish/beasts/birds, flower garlands, pearls and gems, flagstaff and pennons, tiger-skins, the four named horses, Garuda on the flagstaff
obscure timekeeping dropped: 'the hour called Maitra' and 'the constellation Revati' (the next story's opener already carries Kartika/Revati); month Kartika and dew-season kept
'Sini's grandson' (Satyaki) and 'Suvala's son' (Shakuni) and 'Kesava' rendered by plain names
child_friendly_changes: opening anchor: Krishna is the brothers' cousin and friend carrying their plea to Hastinapura; parties of the dispute named in Arjuna's speech
morning rites kept act by act in concrete terms (bath, sun and sacred fire, bull's tail, brahmins' blessing, walking round the fire)

'the fire of universal dissolution' rendered 'the fire that ends a world'; Meru dropped as simile ('high as a mountain'); Garuda glossed 'king of the birds'; Yadavas glossed 'Krishna's own people'; Karna glossed 'the great bowman at his side'
escort named (Bhima, Arjuna, the twins Nakula and Sahadeva, the allied kings) so the send-off reads clearly
risk: Acceptance quote kept its exact three clauses (righteousness -> 'what is right'; beneficial to us -> 'what may benefit us'; good of the Kurus). Weapons order kept complete (conch, discus, mace, quivers, darts, 'every weapon of attack and defence') with the reason: 'even a contemptible enemy should never be underrated by a strong man'. Chariot blaze kept as end-of-world fire simile; no ornament or horse name lost.

ai_patterns_removed: ornamental sage catalogue trimmed: 'Vasishtha and Vamadeva, Bhuridyumna and Gaya, Kratha and Sukra, Kusika and Bhrigu, and many another brahmarishi and celestial sage' -> 'Vasishtha and Vamadeva, with many another sage of earth and heaven' (event unchanged; unglossed 'brahmarishi' removed with it)
'the wishes of Kesava' -> 'Krishna's wishes'; 'Sini's grandson' patronymic dropped (Satyaki now 'his kinsman')
'like a celestial car coursing at the will of its rider' merged into 'moved as if at the rider's will'; 'the flagstaff rattled terribly' -> 'it rattled under his weight'
child_friendly_changes: 'the twin sons of Madri' -> 'the twins Nakula and Sahadeva'; 'Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti' -> plain 'Yudhishthira' (maternal names unexplained in this story)

Karna and Shakuni glossed by role ('the great bowman at his side', 'who rolled the dice against Yudhishthira'); Hastinapura glossed 'the city of the Kurus'; Garuda 'king of the birds'; Yadavas 'Krishna's own people'; 'mantras' -> 'prayers'
opening and closing left intact — this story already opened close to the event and closed on the wheels' sound
risk: Dropped the extra sage names (Bhuridyumna, Gaya, Kratha, Sukra, Kusika, Bhrigu) — an ornamental roll of figures who appear nowhere else in the corpus; Vasishtha and Vamadeva kept. Chariot ornaments, four horses, omens, and the full escort list otherwise preserved.

ai_patterns_removed: single archaic word naturalized: 'who is endued with great wisdom' -> 'who is full of great wisdom' (Vidura salute)

final recap of Krishna's own promise smoothed: 'desirous of accomplishing what was consistent with righteousness, what might be beneficial to the Pandavas, and what was also for the good of the Kurus' -> 'seeking what was right, what might benefit the Pandavas, and what was good for the Kurus'
child_friendly_changes: 'the twins of Madri' -> 'the twins Nakula and Sahadeva' (mother's name unexplained in this story)
'the mighty car-warrior Sikhandin' -> 'the warrior Sikhandin' (epithet trimmed, role kept)

elders' introductions (Kunti as mother who stayed behind, blind Dhritarashtra, Bhishma bound by vow, teachers Drona and Kripa, Vidura the wise uncle) already present in the draft and left intact — the story already stood alone
